English, as the official language and medium of instruction in academic institutions, continues to hold the status of the language of prestige, while Krio is perceived to be an inferior form of English and believed to have a negative influence on the development of English, since it was assumed that Krio speakers will transfer Krio linguistic properties in their use of English.

spans.text: The Liberated Africans were from multiple regions in West Africa, though most of them originated from regions where Yoruba, Igbo, Akan, and Gbe were the predominant languages.
Huber (1999, 2000) proposes that Krio emerged from varieties of creoles used primarily by four groups of settlers, who were freed slaves primarily from four areas.

Creole languages from the West Indies, particularly the variety brought by the Jamaican Maroon settlers, are proposed (Huber 1999) to have had significant input into what has evolved into present-day Krio.

spans.text: The final group – the Liberated Africans (or Recaptives) – were mainly recaptured would-be slaves from slave ships intercepted by the British fleet patrolling the West African coast that were released and resettled in the Sierra Leone peninsula.

There is evidence of British settlement on the Upper Guinea Coast and written reports of interaction, including intermarriages, between Europeans and Africans during this period.
